title: Chet Chetter's Tales from the Morgue
paragraphs: Modern old-radio-style audio theater created by Mark Sawyer and Jay Reel, not a Golden Age series. Nineteen frozen tracks belong to Tales From The Morgue (1989-1992 source-tag years); two later frozen tracks are tagged M & J Presents (1993-1994) and are retained as collection spillover rather than rewritten as original-series episodes.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Tales from the Morgue production period (1989 to 1992), NPR Playhouse broadcast/commission period (1990 to 1992) on [[org|org.dc66a055556c8140|National Public Radio]], and M&J Presents collection spillover (1993 to 1994).
Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Jay Reel (performer).

The stories often return to modern old-radio revival audio theater, supernatural and macabre situations, science fiction and bizarre technology, absurdist and dark comedy, Biloxi / Deep South setting and dialect, and horror-host framing and Inner Sanctum homage.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Modern old-time-radio revival production, M&J Presents expansion beyond Tales From The Morgue, The Highway of Death launches the Chet Chetter project, and Initial NPR Playhouse acceptance and broadcast.
